title.narrative: Activity under preparation Improving Ecuador's investment climate and energy transition

description.narrative: Ecuador is currently facing an energy crisis owing to a paralysis in investment in the sector over a decade, limited openness to private sector participation and non-sustainable tariff systems. This crisis was brought to the forefront by a recent episode of unprecedented electricity rationing in 2024, with daily power cuts reaching up to 14 hours. While this crisis was triggered by an acute drought affecting hydroelectric reservoirs, which supply between 70 and 80% of the country¿s electricity generation; it exposed deeper, long-standing structural weaknesses. . Against this backdrop, and in the context of a newly elected administration that has shown a clear political will to attract foreign direct investment and pursue strategic partnerships with Europe, this Action seeks to support Ecuador in its transition toward a more sustainable, diversified, and resilient energy system. It aligns with Ecuador¿s urgent need to secure a stable and modern electricity supply, while responding to the European Union¿s priority of advancing clean energy investments and regional energy integration under the Global Gateway strategy (REI)This Action proposes to support a clean energy transition in Ecuador, and will have two components: a)Support the improvement of the investment climate with a focus on attracting European foreign direct investment to strategic sectors. It will address key bottlenecks to investments and support the improvement of a more predictable regulatory environment. It will strengthen governance, transparency, and institutional coordination in the implementation of Ecuador¿s investment protocols and investment facilitation mechanisms.b)Support to strategic investments opportunities for non-traditional renewable sources of energy (solar, wind, geothermal and biomass) and a transition process by improving the energy sector regulatory framework (e.g. tariff structure), carrying out market analysis and supporting a limited number of investment projects to bring them to Financial Investment Decision (FID) in energy generation/transmission/distribution. The project support would be integrated, i.e. feasibility studies, technical/financial studies, investment derisking through blending/equity, in order to facilitate FID.The programme will focus on environmental licenses process, legal certainty, investment protection, transparent contracts, procurement in tendering processes (e.g. alignment with international co-financing standards, requesting ESG policy disclosure, record of accomplishment and international certifications), business visits, and fostering technology transfer and local innovation, with a special focus on clean and renewable energy investments.It will include capacity building, technical assistance, and financial support for European operators and Ecuadorian partners, to enhance their roles in tendering and investment opportunities in the energy sector. This component will be carried out in close collaboration with DG TRADE and DG ENER.
